sentences.en: There is a reasonable assumption we make as we go through life.
sentences.zh: 我们在度过一生时，有一个合理的假设。

sentences.en: Groups act in their own self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 群体行事往往出于自身利益。

sentences.en: Merchants sell things in order to make money.
sentences.zh: 商人出售商品是为了赚钱。

sentences.en: Employers want to hire the best employees.
sentences.zh: 雇主想要雇用最好的员工。

sentences.en: Sports teams want to win matches.
The assumption of self-interest is also the lens through which we understand how individuals behave.
sentences.zh: 这种对自私自利的假设，也是我们理解个人行为的视角。

sentences.en: We can see why someone might lie on a resume in order to get ahead.
sentences.zh: 我们可以理解为什么有人会在简历上撒谎以求飞黄腾达。

sentences.en: We also know that no one would lie on their resume to make themselves look worse.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，没有人会在简历上撒谎把自己写得更糟糕。

sentences.en: When people are accused of wrongdoing, it makes perfect sense that the guilty would claim to be innocent.
sentences.zh: 当人们被指控有不当行为时，有罪者声称自己无辜是完全合乎情理的。

sentences.en: But every ounce of common sense tells us no innocent person would ever confess to doing something wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我们的每一点常识都告诉我们，绝没有任何无辜的人会承认自己做错了事。

sentences.en: We understand as a matter of common sense and intuition that people behave in ways that favor their self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 我们凭常识和直觉理解，人们的行为方式有利于他们的自身利益。

sentences.en: How in God's name does that favor your self-interest?
sentences.zh: 老天爷，这怎么可能符合你的自身利益？

sentences.en: How and why people come to betray their self-interest?
sentences.zh: 人们是如何以及为什么会背叛自己的利益的？

sentences.en: In the sixth grade, Saul Kasson received an assignment from his teacher to write a book report.
sentences.zh: 在六年级时，索尔·卡森收到老师布置的一项作业，要写一篇读书报告。

sentences.en: It took him about a nanosecond to decide to write about his hero, Mickey Mantle.
sentences.zh: 他大约花了不到一纳秒的时间就决定写他的偶像米奇·曼特尔。

sentences.en: I was a huge Yankees fan and I wanted to do a really good job.
sentences.zh: 我是扬基队的超级粉丝，我想把这件事做得非常出色。

sentences.en: The baseball star was not the only object of Saul's affections.
sentences.zh: 这位棒球明星并不是索尔倾注热情的唯一对象。

sentences.en: His sixth grade teacher was up on a pedestal too.
sentences.zh: 他的六年级老师也被高高供奉在神坛上。

sentences.en: I had a crush, to be honest, on Mrs. Avery.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我对艾弗里太太有点迷恋。

sentences.en: I wanted to impress Mrs. Avery.
sentences.zh: 我想给艾弗里太太留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: And so I spent a lot of time on this book report.
sentences.zh: 所以我在这篇读书报告上花了大量时间。

sentences.en: I just remember being excited to get the grade back.
sentences.zh: 我只记得当时拿到成绩时非常激动。

sentences.en: I thought it was a really good paper.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一篇非常棒的论文。

sentences.en: I'd spent a lot of time on it.
sentences.zh: 我在上面花了很多时间。

sentences.en: And when she called me up, she would call people and they'd come up and get their paper.
sentences.zh: 当她叫到我的名字时，她会叫大家上去拿他们的论文。

sentences.en: This was toward the end of the school day.
sentences.zh: 这大约是在上学快要结束的时候。

sentences.en: And I just remember her glaring at me in such a way that I looked at the grade and there was, with a circle around it, a big red F.
sentences.zh: 我只记得她怒视着我，我看着成绩，上面是一个画了圈的巨大的红色F。

sentences.en: And she says, well, you plagiarized it.
He loved Mrs. Avery, and he loved Mickey Mantle, and he had poured his heart and soul into the book report.
sentences.zh: 他爱艾弗里太太，也爱米奇·曼特尔，并且把全部的心血都倾注在了这篇读书报告里。

sentences.en: I didn't want to break out into tears in front of my classmates and in front of her, so I held it together.
sentences.zh: 我不想在同学和她面前哭出来，所以我克制住了自己。

sentences.en: I got home, flicked open the door, there was my mother, and I burst out crying.
sentences.zh: 我回到家，推开门，我妈妈就在那儿，我突然放声大哭起来。

sentences.en: Mrs. Avery accused me of cheating.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里太太指控我作弊。

sentences.en: She didn't ask me if I plagiarized.
sentences.zh: 她没有问我是不是抄袭了。

sentences.en: She told me that I did.
And I just will never forget the helplessness that I felt at having been accused of something I didn't do
sentences.zh: 我永远不会忘记那种无助感，因为我被指控做了我没有做过的事

sentences.en: and not really knowing how to respond in a way to defend myself.
sentences.zh: 却又真的不知道该如何反应来为自己辩护。

sentences.en: It was Saul's mother who finally obtained justice.
sentences.zh: 是索尔的母亲最终伸张了正义。

sentences.en: She demanded proof from Mrs. Avery that the book report was plagiarized.
sentences.zh: 她要求艾弗里太太提供这篇读书报告是抄袭的证据。

sentences.en: Mrs. Avery looked for evidence but couldn't find any, so she changed Saul's grade.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里太太寻找证据却找不到，于是她更改了索尔的成绩。

sentences.en: But the moment of helplessness stayed with Saul.
sentences.zh: 但那种无助的时刻一直留在索尔心中。

sentences.en: Why had he been unable to speak up?
sentences.zh: 为什么他当时无法开口说话？

sentences.en: Saul grew up to become a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 索尔长大后成为了一名心理学家。

sentences.en: How people interpret the actions of others.
sentences.zh: 人们如何解读他人的行为。

sentences.en: He was especially fascinated by juries.
Here were people whose conclusions about defendants had life and death stakes.
sentences.zh: 这里有一群人，他们对被告的定论关乎生死存亡。

sentences.en: To evaluate the psychological factors that shape how juries think,
sentences.zh: 为了评估塑造陪审团思维的心理因素，

sentences.en: Saul came up with cases where some jurors might feel a defendant was guilty,
sentences.zh: 索尔设计了一些案件，在这些案件中，一些陪审员可能会觉得被告有罪，

sentences.en: while others might feel he was innocent.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人可能会觉得他是无辜的。

sentences.en: Saul figured ambiguous cases would shed light on how people make up their minds about guilt and innocence.
sentences.zh: 索尔认为，模棱两可的案件将有助于阐明人们是如何对有罪和无罪做出决定的。

sentences.en: He started running experiments with volunteers playing the role of jurors.
sentences.zh: 他开始让扮演陪审员的志愿者参与实验。

sentences.en: He noticed there were some cases where his volunteers were totally unanimous.
sentences.zh: 他注意到在某些案件中，他的志愿者们完全异口同声。

sentences.en: A couple of cases came back that elicited no variability.
sentences.zh: 有几个案件没有引发任何意见分歧。

sentences.en: As far as everybody was concerned, everybody was guilty.
sentences.zh: 在所有人看来，每个人都有罪。

sentences.en: Fortunately, we also asked subjects in those studies to explain their verdict.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们还要求这些研究中的受试者解释他们的裁决。

sentences.en: What was the basis for your verdict?
sentences.zh: 你做出裁决的依据是什么？

sentences.en: And in the cases that I recall, everybody cited a confession.
sentences.zh: 在我记得的案件中，每个人都提到了口供。

sentences.en: When a defendant in a criminal case admitted he had done something wrong,
sentences.zh: 当刑事案件中的被告承认自己做错了事时，

sentences.en: volunteers playing the role of jurors saw these as open and shut cases.
sentences.zh: 扮演陪审员角色的志愿者就会认为这些是板上钉钉的铁案。
那他们显然就是有罪的。

sentences.en: My first response was, well, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是，嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: It looks like we'll have to remove confessions from evidence in order to use cases.
sentences.zh: 看来我们必须从证据中排除口供才能使用这些案件。

sentences.en: Saul wanted cases where volunteers disagreed with each other.
sentences.zh: 索尔想要志愿者们意见不一的案件。

sentences.en: Cases involving confessions, where everyone agreed with everyone else, were useless.
sentences.zh: 涉及口供、每个人意见完全一致的案件毫无用处。

sentences.en: So right away, we tossed out cases involving confessions because confessions were a nuisance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们立刻抛弃了涉及口供的案件，因为口供是个干扰因素。

sentences.en: It happens so often in science as well as in life.
sentences.zh: 这在科学界和生活中都经常发生。

sentences.en: We fail to notice something important because we are so intent on something else.
sentences.zh: 我们因为过于专注于某事而忽视了重要的事情。

sentences.en: It took Saul a while to realize his nuisance was telling him something important.
sentences.zh: 索尔花了好一阵子才意识到，他的干扰因素正在向他传达重要信息。

sentences.en: As he continued to study juries, Saul decided he needed to better understand how police procured evidence in criminal trials.
sentences.zh: 随着他对陪审团研究的深入，索尔决定他需要更好地了解警方在刑事审判中是如何获取证据的。

sentences.en: He decided to audit a law school class on evidence.
sentences.zh: 他决定去旁听一节法学院的证据法课程。

sentences.en: And there was a footnote in that casebook in which they referenced an interrogation manual, the most popular interrogation manual.
sentences.zh: 在那本案例汇编中有一个脚注，里面参考了一本审讯手册，即最受欢迎的审讯手册。

sentences.en: So I thought, wow, how interesting to see what they're doing to interrogate.
sentences.zh: 于是我想，哇，看看他们在审讯中做些什么，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: And so I went to the library and pulled out that edition of that manual, and I read the book.
sentences.zh: 于是我去了图书馆，翻出了那本手册的那个版本，并读了这本书。

sentences.en: What kind of techniques were in this manual, Saul?
sentences.zh: 这本手册里都有哪些技术，索尔？

sentences.en: Well, for starters, the opening salvo of an interrogation was to bring in a suspect and declare an accusation of guilt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，审讯的开场白就是把嫌疑人带进来，并宣称他有罪。

sentences.en: This, of course, is exactly what Mrs. Avery had done in the sixth grade.
sentences.zh: 这当然正是艾弗里太太在六年级时做过的事。

sentences.en: In fact, I believe in that first manual, they advised the interrogator to come in with a folder full of materials and toss it on the table and said,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我记得在那本最初的手册中，他们建议审讯人员带一个装满材料的文件夹进来，把它扔在桌子上说，

sentences.en: we've got a lot of evidence against you.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了大量对你不利的证据。

sentences.en: And they suggested doing that even if you didn't have a whole lot of evidence.
sentences.zh: 他们建议即使你并没有很多证据，也要这么做。

sentences.en: So right out of the gate, I'm looking and I'm saying, OK, wow, these are powerful tactics.
sentences.zh: 所以刚一开局，我就看着并心想，好吧，哇，这些真是强力战术。
这些简直带有米尔格拉姆实验的风格。

sentences.en: In the early 1960s, Stanley Milgram conducted a series of experiments on blind obedience.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代初，斯坦利·米尔格拉姆进行了一系列关于盲目服从的实验。

sentences.en: He tested if volunteers would comply with instructions from an authority figure.
sentences.zh: 他测试志愿者是否会遵从权威人士的指示。

sentences.en: The most famous experiment featured an experimenter who demanded that a volunteer subject someone else to painful electric shocks.
sentences.zh: 最著名的实验有一个实验员，他要求一名志愿者对另一个人实施痛苦的电击。

sentences.en: In reality, no one received shocks.
sentences.zh: 实际上，没有人真的受到电击。

sentences.en: The experiment was designed to test if volunteers were willing to go along with crazy instructions.
sentences.zh: 该实验旨在测试志愿者是否愿意顺从疯狂的指令。

sentences.en: If the volunteer resisted, the experimenter had a series of verbal prods to keep the experiment going.
sentences.zh: 如果志愿者反抗，实验员有一系列言语催促来让实验继续下去。

sentences.en: It's absolutely essential that you continue.
sentences.zh: 你继续下去是绝对必要的。

sentences.en: You have no other choice, teacher.
The experiment requires that you continue.
And the prods are designed to get a subject to first administer a 15-volt shock and then a 30-volt shock.
sentences.zh: 这些催促旨在让受试者首先施加15伏的电击，然后是30伏的电击。

sentences.en: And in 15-volt increments to bring that subject up to the point where they would be asked to administer a 450-volt shock,
sentences.zh: 并以15伏的增幅，引导该受试者达到被要求实施450伏电击的程度，

sentences.en: which on Milgram's shock machine was listed as XXX severe shock.
sentences.zh: 在米尔格拉姆的电击机上，这被列为XXX严重电击。

sentences.en: When you look at this paradigm, you go, nobody's going to do that.
sentences.zh: 当你看到这个范式时，你会想，没有人会这么做。

sentences.en: Well, we're going on if he refuses to do it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他拒绝这么做，我们将继续进行。

sentences.en: The experiment requires that you go on, teacher.
65% of subjects go all the way up the shock scale to 450 volts.
sentences.zh: 65%的受试者一直把电击等级拉到了最高的450伏。
这就是米尔格拉姆实验。

sentences.en: Now I look at the interrogation manual.
You bring them in, isolated, no friends or family members or lawyers present.
sentences.zh: 你把他们带进来，进行隔离，没有朋友、家人或律师在场。

sentences.en: There is instead of an experimenter as an authority figure, a police detective who has real authority.
sentences.zh: 作为权威人物的不是实验员，而是一名拥有真实权力的警探。

sentences.en: And that police detective aims to accuse you of something and get you to make an admission of guilt.
sentences.zh: 那位警探的目标是控告你某项罪名，并让你承认有罪。

sentences.en: And through a process of gradual escalation and a series of prods that are listed,
sentences.zh: 通过逐渐升级的过程和列出的一系列催促，

sentences.en: the detective's goal is to get you to make a small confession or an admission of, I was there.
sentences.zh: 警探的目标是让你做一个小的供认或承认“我在现场”。

sentences.en: And then a slightly greater admission, I saw what happened.
sentences.zh: 然后是一个稍大一点的承认：“我看到了发生的事。”

sentences.en: And then a slightly greater admission, I was minimally involved.
sentences.zh: 再然后是一个更大的承认：“我只是轻度参与。”

sentences.en: And eventually, 15 volts at a time, the goal is to get that person to make a full admission of guilt,
sentences.zh: 最终，一次增加15伏，其目标是让那个人完全承认有罪，

sentences.en: coupled by a full narrative confession that explains the chronology and the story.
sentences.zh: 并配以解释时间线和故事的完整叙述性口供。

sentences.en: The authority figure in Milgram's obedience experiment, it's a psychology experimenter wearing a white lab coat
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆服从实验中的权威人物，是一个穿着白色实验服的心理学实验员，

sentences.en: who has no real authority and no real power over those subjects.
sentences.zh: 他对那些受试者没有真正的权威，也没有真正的权力。

sentences.en: If an authority figure like a psych experimenter can produce that level of obedience,
sentences.zh: 如果像心理学实验员这样的权威人物能够产生那种程度的服从，

sentences.en: can you imagine what a detective who has power over your fate and future might be able to produce?
sentences.zh: 你能想象一个对你的命运和未来拥有权力的警探能制造出什么样的结果吗？
这就是让我感到不安的地方。

sentences.en: I kept thinking, geez, if they bring innocent people into this situation,
sentences.zh: 我一直在想，天哪，如果他们把无辜的人带入这种境地，

sentences.en: they're going to get some Milgram-like results.
sentences.zh: 他们会得到一些类似米尔格拉姆实验的结果。

sentences.en: Saul realized he was confronting two powerful facts.
sentences.zh: 索尔意识到他正在面对两个强有力的事实。

sentences.en: Fact number one, juries believe people when they offer confessions.
sentences.zh: 事实一：陪审团相信人们提供的口供。

sentences.en: Fact number two, police are taught to extract confessions from people
sentences.zh: 事实二：警方被教导如何从人们那里逼出口供，

sentences.en: using a series of powerful psychological techniques.
sentences.zh: 他们使用的是一系列强大的心理技术。

sentences.en: You don't have to assume bad intent on the part of detectives for this to be a problem.
sentences.zh: 要让这成为一个问题，你并不需要假设警探怀有恶意。

sentences.en: Like the rest of us, detectives assume no one who is innocent will admit to being guilty.
sentences.zh: 和我们其余人一样，警探们假设没有哪个无辜的人会承认自己有罪。

sentences.en: Saul decided to look more closely at the science of confessions.
sentences.zh: 索尔决定更仔细地研究口供科学。

sentences.en: Only, he found, there was no science of confessions.
sentences.zh: 只是他发现，根本没有什么口供科学。

sentences.en: When someone says they did something wrong,
sentences.zh: 当有人说他们做错了事时，

sentences.en: it seems so self-evidently obvious that they did do something wrong
sentences.zh: 这看起来如此不言自明，以至于他们确实做错了事，

sentences.en: that no one had really studied it.
sentences.zh: 以至于根本没有人真正研究过它。

sentences.en: Saul did find one early example, though,
sentences.zh: 不过，索尔确实找到了一个早期的例子，

sentences.en: a case study described in the early 20th century
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪初由一位名叫雨果·芒斯特伯格的心理学家

sentences.en: by a psychologist named Hugo Munsterberg.
sentences.zh: 所描述的一个案例研究。

sentences.en: Munsterberg has a chapter titled Untrue Confessions,
sentences.zh: 芒斯特伯格有一个章节名为《虚假口供》，

sentences.en: and in it he describes this case out of Chicago,
sentences.zh: 并在其中描述了芝加哥的这个案件，
即贝茜·霍利斯特谋杀案。

sentences.en: and what I think made him skeptical about the confession,
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是让他对那份供词产生怀疑的原因，

sentences.en: and was a vulnerable person to issue as a suspect.
sentences.zh: 而且在被列为嫌疑人这件事上属于弱势群体。

sentences.en: He then realized that they then brought him in for hours of interrogation,
sentences.zh: 他随后意识到，警方对嫌疑人进行了长达数小时的审讯，

sentences.en: in which it was described that he embellished a story
sentences.zh: 据描述，他在审讯过程中添油加醋，
每次讲述时细节都不一样。

sentences.en: Turns out he provided some details in that story,
sentences.zh: 结果证明他在那段讲述中提供了一些细节，

sentences.en: and it turns out that some of those details were false.
sentences.zh: 而事实证明其中部分细节是假的。

sentences.en: And so, we have a situation
sentences.zh: 因此，我们遇到了这样一种情况：

sentences.en: where he was interrogated for long periods of time,
sentences.zh: 他接受了长时间的审讯，
他是一个弱势的嫌疑人，

sentences.en: in relation to the case facts.
And yet, the prosecutor pushed forward,
sentences.zh: 然而，检察官却执意推进，

sentences.en: and within, I kid you not,

sentences.zh: 短短一周内他就被定罪了。

sentences.en: And shortly thereafter, he was hung.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，他就被绞死了。

sentences.en: Saul started looking for other cases
sentences.zh: 索尔开始在历史记录中寻找

sentences.en: of untrue confessions in the history books.
Eventually, he came up with a classification system.
sentences.zh: 最终，他提出了一套分类系统。

sentences.en: The first kind were voluntary false confessions,
sentences.zh: 第一种是自愿型虚假供词，

sentences.en: when a famous aviator's son was kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 当时一位著名飞行员的儿子被绑架了。

sentences.en: Charles Lindbergh was, at the time,
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·林德伯格在当时

sentences.en: and his infant son was kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 而他襁褓中的儿子被绑架了。

sentences.en: And it was big news, as you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这成了轰动一时的新闻。
结果有200人主动跑来招认

sentences.en: And ultimately, police did not charge any of them.
sentences.zh: 最终，警方没有起诉其中任何一个人。

sentences.en: Ultimately, none of them had anything to do with it.
